messages:
Ellen: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC push, SCIM deprovisioning is flapping for oracle-corp org. Getting 403 on the provisioning callback and IdP logs show an 'aud' claim mismatch for the OIDC client we rotated. Seen any KMS errors around the same time?
Sasha: I see KMS decrypt errors around 03:12 UTC — some InvalidCiphertextException spikes from alias/redwood/idp-key. Might be unrelated but timing aligns.
Kevin: Quick audit check: provisioning events include two client_ids: `web-app-client-v2` and `web-app-client`. Looks like the old client_id is still referenced by the SCIM integration.
Ellen: We rotated the oauth client (changed client_id + secret) to break a long-lived secret. Sounds like SCIM config wasn't updated -> aud mismatch. Also noticed a ~30s hole in our audit pipeline (ELB rotate) where events are missing. Triage suggestions?
Sasha: Proposed immediate actions: 1) temporarily accept old client_id as aud on gateway, 2) run SCIM in probe mode to capture retries, 3) investigate KMS error source and re-encrypt any affected payloads.
Kevin: I'm adding old client_id to allowed audience on the gateway now. @idp-bot can you apply the change?
idp-bot: gateway config updated: `gateway.aud.whitelist += web-app-client` (applied by idp-bot)
Maria: KMS team — the decrypt errors line up with a rekey job that ran 03:12 UTC. One key version failed propagation to the staging endpoint; I'm requeueing re-encrypt for objects that failed.
Ellen: Also seeing duplicate service accounts for some users (extId collisions). SCIM likely retried creates during the aud mismatch window. We'll need to reconcile and prune duplicates and merge attributes like last_active.
Kevin: Exported recent SCIM events for triage: s3://redwood-incident-logs/scim/1788888000-export.csv
Sasha: Running probe sync now, snippet: \n```\n[2026-03-18T03:40:12Z] scim-sync: 409 Conflict -> user exists (extId=user:oracle:1234)\n[2026-03-18T03:40:13Z] scim-sync: 201 Created -> user (repaired duplicate by appending -dup)\n```\nSo the sync created fallback duplicates instead of linking — bug in idempotency.
Maria: Re-encrypt job finished, KMS errors cleared. Still finding the root of the secret leak — where did the client secret end up?
Ellen: Found it: an internal debug job wrote a dump to S3 that included `oauth_client_secret` in plaintext. That job had overly broad S3 perms. Vulnerability triage: rotate secret, purge the S3 object, restrict job IAM perms, and audit other tool logs for secrets.
Kevin: Rotating client secret now. I'll update IdP app and SCIM config in the maintenance window and revoke refresh tokens to invalidate sessions.
Sasha: Before rotation, I'll push a small change to SCIM to make create idempotent by checking extId first and linking instead of creating. Quick PR incoming.
Ellen: Good. Postmortem actions to capture: 1) fail CI if debug uploads contain sensitive keys, 2) require coordinated change for client_id rotations (SCIM + gateway + IdP), 3) improve audit pipeline to avoid 30s holes, 4) add KMS alert for InvalidCiphertextException >5 in 5m.
Maria: Filed INF-421 to reduce S3 write perms for dev/debug jobs and to purge the leaked object. Also added a KMS alert rule and will run a re-encrypt sweep for any remaining failed items.
Kevin: After secret rotation and re-encrypt + SCIM fix, probe sync shows no new duplicates in the last hour. Looks stable from my side.
Ellen: Hold for 24h monitoring, then remove the aud whitelist entry once all clients report OK. Add to oncall checklist: verify audit gaps closed and duplicate cleanup finished.
Kevin: :thumbsup: will follow up and post an update to the incident channel when we remove the temp whitelist.
